name: Grand Hyatt Taipei
positioning: Large city hotel next door to Taipei 101, with a bridge connecting directly to the tower, Taipei 101 views and an outdoor pool
best_for: Travelers who want to stay right beside Taipei 101 with views of the tower
Guests who want club-lounge access or a large suite with a kitchenette

facts.text: Major public transportation is a five-minute walk from the hotel.
The nearest MRT station is Taipei 101/World Trade Center.
Guest rooms are designed with a residential touch.
Condé Nast Traveler notes the hotel's pastel rooms.
The Grand Executive 101 View Suite has a Taipei 101 view, a living room and a bedroom, a marble bathroom with a bathtub, and Grand Club Lounge access.
Executive suites have marble tubs from which guests can watch Taipei 101 light up at sunset.
The Diplomat Suite has a separate living area, a kitchenette, a walk-in closet and a marble bathroom.
Club Oasis has a 24-hour fitness center and an exercise studio with classes such as yoga and aerobics.
Club Oasis has separate men's and women's wet areas with a sauna, steam room and whirlpools.
Pearl Liang serves Cantonese cuisine in a private-residence-style setting by designer Tony Chi.
At Café, a team of 30 chefs cooks Asian specialties in a show kitchen.
Pets are welcome, with a pet-friendly package of rooms, amenities and services designed for dogs.

highlights.text: The hotel has a bridge that connects directly to Taipei 101.
Rooms and suites look out on Taipei 101, Taiwan's tallest skyscraper, right next door, as well as other city views.
The temperature-controlled outdoor pool on level 5 is set in lush landscaping, with sun beds, lounge areas and a pool bar.
The Grand Club Lounge on the 22nd floor has panoramic views of the Taipei skyline, with continental breakfast, all-day refreshments and an evening cocktail experience.
The Presidential Suite is an apartment-style suite with a 24-hour private butler.

considerations.text: The hotel no longer provides bottled water or disposable in-room amenities, so bring your own essentials and a drinking vessel.
WhataHotel notes the busy urban setting may not suit travelers seeking tranquility.
WhataHotel notes premium pricing reflecting the hotel's luxury positioning.

sources.title: Conde Nast Traveler: Grand Hyatt Taipei
